procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 11.11.2014 of the High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur in CRLA No. 529 of 2008.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur issued a Judgment and Order dated 11.11.2014 in CRLA No. 529 of 2008. The outcome of this order is not explicitly stated in the provided text, but it was challenged in the Supreme Court.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellants approached the Supreme Court by filing SLP(Criminal) Nos. 6134-6135 of 2019, in which leave to appeal was granted. The Supreme Court then heard Criminal Appeal No. 1421 of 2015, along with Criminal Appeal Nos. 1470 of 2017 and 775-776 of 2023. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals, effectively overturning the High Court's decision.

directions: The appellants are directed to be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other case.

issue.issue_text: Whether the timeline of the incident as per the FIR, stating that the incident occurred at 8:30 PM and the injured persons reached the Bazar around 10-11 PM, is believable.

facts: The FIR stated that the incident occurred at approximately 8:30 PM.
The FIR also stated that the injured persons reached the Bazar between 10:00 PM and 11:00 PM.
application: The Supreme Court did not challenge the timeline of the incident occurring at 8:30 PM and the injured arriving at the Bazar between 10-11 PM.
Instead, the Court explicitly stated that it was "believing" and "assuming" this timeline to be correct for the purpose of its analysis.

The Court used this accepted timeline as a starting point to highlight a different, more significant issue: the subsequent unexplained delay of four to five hours in lodging the FIR after the injured had already reached the Bazar.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the timeline presented in the FIR not because it was proven, but as a premise for its argument. By accepting these facts as true, the Court was able to demonstrate that even under the prosecution's own timeline, there was a subsequent, unexplained delay in filing the official report, which cast serious doubt on the genuineness of the prosecution's case.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the timeline of the incident as per the FIR, stating that the incident occurred at 8:30 PM and the injured persons reached the Bazar around 10-11 PM, is believable.
appellant_arguments: While not explicitly stated in the provided text, the appellant's argument can be inferred from the respondent's counter-argument. The appellant likely argued that the delay in lodging the FIR, evidenced by the questionable timeline of the incident occurring at 8:30 PM and the injured only reaching the Bazar between 10-11 PM, casts doubt on the credibility of the prosecution's case.
respondent_arguments: Merely because there is some delay in lodging the FIR, it cannot be a ground to discard the prosecution case, which has been proved beyond reasonable doubt.
